proposal.summary: Both current winners still earn their specific roles on verified evidence, but merit-not-incumbency review finds their pins verifiably stale in ways that matter for this layer's own "deterministic numeric risk" requirement. skfolio (pinned 1.2.9) is 6 releases behind live upstream v1.4.0 (independently confirmed via gh api release list, correcting the researcher packet's "two releases" undercount): v1.3.1/1.3.2/1.3.3/1.3.4 are risk-measure bug fixes (plotting crash, sample-weight preservation, VaR tail-size consistency, EVaR numerical stability), read directly from each release body today. A PR (#81) already native-execution-qualified 1.3.0 on 2026-09-23 (Sharpe/weights reproduced to reported precision) but manifests/stack.json still pins 1.2.9 -- the qualification was never promoted. edgartools (pinned v5.58.0) is 2 releases behind v5.59.1 (also correcting the packet's miscount), and v5.59.1 fixes a total-failure bug where 13F holdings always returned None. Separately, a 2026-09-23 internal sweep for this exact layer -- reconfirmed live today via gh api -- already found two adversarially-verified, currently-active candidates (LightGBM, RD-Agent) closing a real gap this layer's own open_gaps admit is uncovered (no factor-IC tool, no automated factor/model-research loop, no GBDT engine despite known dependents Qlib/ML4T using one). That same sweep already refuted the packet's own framing of AlphaGen (stronger grounds: unlicensed, dormant since Dec 2024, China-only data) and downgraded Kronos (overlaps two already-catalogued forecasting baselines). All candidates here are research/evaluation tooling only; paper orders remain confined to the deterministic adaptive-paper engine.

winner_status.note: Still the best-evidenced WalkForward/portfolio-optimization library for this role; no verified alternative beats it (Riskfolio-Lib is a legitimate but untested head-to-head, see challengers). Independently confirmed today via gh api that upstream shipped v1.3.0..v1.4.0 (6 releases) since the 1.2.9 pin, correcting the researcher packet's own undercount of 'two releases'. Read the actual release bodies: v1.3.1 fixes a plotting crash (PR #330), v1.3.2 fixes sample-weight preservation across multi-period updates (PR #338), v1.3.3 fixes value_at_risk consistency at integer tail sizes (PR #343), v1.3.4 fixes EVaR numerical stability via log-sum-exp (PR #359) -- risk-measure correctness fixes, not cosmetic, directly inside this layer's own 'deterministic numeric risk' requirement. evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260923/pins-runtime/skfolio.json (native_proven, read directly) shows a merged PR (#81, merged 2026-09-23) already reran the WalkForward acceptance on 1.3.0 and reproduced the 1.2.9 receipt's Sharpe/weights to reported precision, yet manifests/stack.json still pins 1.2.9 today -- the qualification was never promoted to the tracked pin. Action: bump the pin to >=1.3.4 (ideally 1.4.0) and extend the same reproduction, since the skipped point releases are risk-measure bug fixes.

Still the best-evidenced SEC-filing acquisition/parsing SDK; FinanceToolkit was checked for this exact role on 2026-09-23 and found to demonstrate no gap over it. Independently confirmed today via gh api release list that only v5.59.0 and v5.59.1 postdate the v5.58.0 pin (v5.57.0 predates it, correcting the researcher packet's claim of 'three releases past the pin' to the actual two). v5.59.1's release body fixes edgar_read() returning no 13F holdings section for any filing (GH #1337, a total-failure bug, not an edge case) and a 10-K Item 7 breadcrumb mis-open regression introduced in 5.59.0. Any catalyst/filing research reusing this pin for 13F-derived signals is currently affected. Action: bump the pin to 5.59.1 and re-run the existing acquisition/parsing fixture before relying on 13F output.

challengers.name: LightGBM (lightgbm-org/LightGBM)
challengers.why_better: Closes a real, verified gap: this layer's own known dependents (microsoft/qlib -- confirmed today by reading its pyproject.toml, which lists 'lightgbm' as a direct dependency -- and stefan-jansen/machine-learning-for-trading) use LightGBM as their central tabular-ML model for factor-based return prediction, yet no gradient-boosted-tree engine is itself a tracked component; scikit-learn's tree ensembles are not what those known repos' own benchmark results use. A 2026-09-23 internal sweep for this exact layer ran two independent adversarial-verification lenses and both survived (non-refuted, high confidence); re-confirmed live today via gh api MIT, 18,814 stars, pushed 2026-09-25 (yesterday), latest release v4.7.0 (2026-07-18); microsoft/LightGBM now redirects to lightgbm-org/LightGBM, confirming the March-2026 org move the sweep flagged.
challengers.trial_plan: Using the already-frozen WalkForward folds from blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/ (same purge/embargo inputs as the skfolio acceptance), fit LightGBM's LGBMRegressor against scikit-learn's HistGradientBoostingRegressor on an identical factor panel and forward-return target on the same folds. Compare development-fold IC/rank-IC, training wall-clock at this panel's actual scale, and reserved-segment Sharpe net of costs. Pass criterion to adopt: LightGBM must beat HistGradientBoostingRegressor's IC/Sharpe outside noise at comparable wall-clock; parity or a scikit-learn win means keep scikit-learn and drop the new dependency.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none -- a research/model-selection step upstream of any strategy; models stay in research per this layer's own scope, so this cannot move engines run, paper acts passed or paper fills.

challengers.name: RD-Agent (microsoft/RD-Agent)
challengers.why_better: None of this layer's tracked candidates automate the factor+model research loop itself; a human still designs factors/models manually on top of Qlib. RD-Agent(Q) is Microsoft's own actively developed agentic layer performing exactly that, with a self-reported (unverified on this project's data) ~2x annualized-return improvement using >70% fewer factors, presented at NeurIPS 2025. A 2026-09-23 internal sweep ran two-lens adversarial verification and both survived (non-refuted); re-confirmed live today: MIT, 14,758 stars, pushed 2026-09-23, latest release v1.0.0 (2026-09-23, mature -- 12 prior 0.6-0.8 releases preceded it).
challengers.trial_plan: On this project's own point-in-time equity universe and purged/embargoed folds, run RD-Agent(Q)'s automated factor+model co-evolution for a fixed wall-clock/compute budget against a human-run Qlib LGBModel baseline. Critical correction the internal review already flagged (citing feedback.py:17-20,110): RD-Agent's own feedback loop scores the test segment's IC/ARR during evolution, so that segment is not a real holdout -- reserve a further final segment the loop never scores at all, and score both the evolved output and the human baseline on it exactly once, after evolution finishes: IC, realized Sharpe net of costs, factor count. Pass criterion: beat the human baseline net of its own compute cost on that untouched segment, or reproduce a return/factor-count advantage near its published claim on this project's actual panel. Note its default templates hard-code cn/csi300 (GH issue #1366) -- expect real retargeting work before any comparison is meaningful.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none directly -- an automated research loop upstream of any order; could over time increase qualified signals reaching a future paper strategy, but moves no current paper-lane counter by itself.

challengers.name: alphalens-reloaded (stefan-jansen/alphalens-reloaded)
challengers.why_better: Fills an explicitly open gap this layer's own open_gaps list names: no factor-IC/quantile-return/turnover tear-sheet tooling exists in this catalog, the standard complement to skfolio's portfolio-construction role. It is the maintained continuation of quantopian/alphalens, which is confirmed stale (pushed 2024-02-12, >2.5 years). Caveat, not a strength: it is itself only marginally maintained -- pushed 2025-12-15 (~9.4 months ago, inside the 12-month rule but slowing), last PyPI upload 0.4.6 on 2025-06-02 (>15 months), and the 2026-09-23 internal sweep already flagged it 'unmaintained_signal' for a stale default-branch head. No fresher alternative for this specific niche was found.
challengers.trial_plan: Run its factor tear-sheet/IC function against the same frozen factor panel and reserved segment already scored in blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/receipt.json (e.g. the momentum20 diagnostic), under the pinned Python/pandas/numpy already in that venv. Cross-check its printed IC against a hand-computed Spearman rank correlation on the identical folds. Pass criterion: installs and runs without error under the current pins and its IC matches the manual computation within floating-point tolerance. If it errors under the current pins (a real risk given its slowing cadence) or its IC diverges, treat the gap as still open rather than adopting it as-is.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none -- a research/evaluation diagnostic (factor IC), not order generation or fills.

challengers.name: Riskfolio-Lib (dcajasn/Riskfolio-Lib)
challengers.why_better: No verified performance advantage over skfolio exists yet -- stating that plainly rather than overclaiming. What is verified: it is an already-catalog-pinned (repository-index.md:142, engines-strategies.json commit 632a9e48fbaf2b9f8e83864a492332364b6ed32c), actively maintained (pushed 2026-09-24, 2 days before this research), BSD-3-Clause, non-archived direct competitor for skfolio's own portfolio-optimization/risk-parity role -- and it is the exact comparison this layer's own overturn_when clause calls for ('Compare alternatives on the same frozen inputs and failure contract'), never executed despite skfolio being pinned since before 2026-09-19. Listed because the comparison is overdue and verifiably available, not because it has been shown to win.
challengers.trial_plan: On the identical frozen SPY/QQQ/IWM inputs and WalkForward split already used in blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/receipt.json, fit Riskfolio-Lib's HRP and mean-risk optimizers alongside skfolio's HierarchicalRiskParity/MeanRisk on the same development and reserved folds. Compare reserved-segment annualized Sharpe/weights and wall-clock. Also check whether Riskfolio-Lib has any purge/embargo-aware cross-validation splitter, since skfolio's own WalkForward purge/embargo currently defaults to zero (a recorded open gap) -- lacking one would itself favor skfolio even with its default unconfigured. Pass criterion to promote: match or beat skfolio's reserved-fold Sharpe within noise AND not regress the purge/embargo fix once it lands. Until run, it stays a documented, available comparison.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none -- a portfolio-construction research comparison, not itself an order or fill.

researched_candidates.name: skfolio
researched_candidates.fit: Current winner. Upstream is healthier than the packet recorded: the open_gap flagged pin 1.2.9 behind v1.3.0, but two releases have since shipped (v1.3.0, v1.4.0 same day). None of the new features (GeodesicShrinkageCovariance, treemap plot) close the layer's real gaps (no portfolio P&L/dividend/fee reconciliation, purge/embargo defaulted to zero, only ETF-sample evidence) -- those are evaluation-design gaps, not upstream-version gaps. Re-pin to 1.4.0 is a routine bump, not an overturn trigger by itself.

researched_candidates.name: EdgarTools
researched_candidates.fit: Current winner. Upstream is 3 patch releases ahead of the pin (v5.58.0 -> v5.59.0 -> v5.59.1) and one of those releases fixes a genuine parsing bug (13F holdings extraction) that would matter for any catalyst/filing-based factor research reusing this library -- worth re-pinning. This does not touch the layer's actual open gaps: the EdgarTools acquisition evidence remains a bounded 5-header, one-day sample and does not establish a historical as-known filing corpus.

researched_candidates.name: Qlib (Microsoft)
researched_candidates.fit: Strong general-purpose factor/ML research platform, but adopting it does not resolve this layer's core blocker (no point-in-time, licensed US-equity universe). Flag: judge Qlib's 'maintained' status by commit activity, not by its release tag -- the tag/PyPI version is stale by the 12-month rule even though the source is not. Any use would still need the same causal-data and independent-reconciliation qualification the overturn_when clause requires.

researched_candidates.name: alphalens-reloaded
researched_candidates.fit: Directly on-topic for factor evaluation (IC, quantile returns, turnover) and complements skfolio's WalkForward evidence with the standard factor-tear-sheet workflow the layer currently lacks. Marginally maintained by the 12-month rule -- worth re-checking in another 3 months before treating it as a settled dependency.

researched_candidates.name: mlfinlab (Hudson & Thames)
researched_candidates.fit: Historically influential and still worth reading as a reference for labeling/feature techniques, but by this task's own rules it must be flagged unmaintained (no commit in ~3 years) with an unclear license and no live open-source PyPI distribution. Not fit for direct adoption; any of its techniques used here should be reimplemented or sourced from a maintained fork, not installed as-is.

researched_candidates.name: AlphaGen
researched_candidates.fit: The strongest awesome-list-sourced example of automated (rather than hand-crafted) factor mining for this layer, and a good complement to skfolio's evaluation-only role. The missing license is a hard blocker for adoption until resolved -- flag before any integration work, independent of maintenance status.

researched_candidates.name: Kronos (financial K-line foundation model)
researched_candidates.fit: Directly relevant as a domain-specific alternative/complement to the already-adopted general-purpose timesfm (google-research/timesfm) forecasting model: if Kronos's self-reported gains over 'the leading TSFM' replicate independently on this stack's data, it is a credible challenger for any forecasting sub-step of factor research. Evidence here is paper-level (source_review of the arXiv listing) plus repo metadata -- no native_execution exists; the packet is correct that this remains untested, not failed, and any promotion needs the same independent, cost-aware evaluation the layer's overturn_when clause requires.

researched_candidates.name: AlphaForge
researched_candidates.fit: Genuinely new-to-this-packet find (not in any of the supplied starred/awesome-list inputs) representing the dynamic-combination branch of automated alpha mining, distinct from AlphaGen's pure-generation approach. Must be flagged unmaintained by this task's 12-month rule despite being a real, peer-reviewed (AAAI 2025) result with working code -- a clean example of a credible paper-with-code that is nonetheless stale as a dependency; usable as a reference implementation to reimplement from, not as a live install.

researched_candidates.name: deepdow
researched_candidates.fit: Conceptually interesting differentiable-allocation approach that would complement skfolio's evaluation-only role, but confirmed unmaintained -- do not adopt as a live dependency without first checking for an actively maintained fork.

researched_candidates.name: Spectre
researched_candidates.fit: The awesome-quant entry undersells how stale this is: last real release tag is nearly 7 years old and the repo itself has had no commits in almost a year and a half. researched_candidates.name: FactorMiner
researched_candidates.fit: The clearest 'beyond stars and awesome lists' find for this layer: none of the supplied starred repos or awesome-list entries surfaced this or the adjacent 2026 LLM-agent alpha-mining wave (AlphaLogics arXiv:2603.20247, AQuA arXiv:2608.12841, Alpha-R1 arXiv:2512.23515, AlphaMemo arXiv:2606.20625, XAlpha arXiv:2607.08332 -- found via the same search but not independently read here, so not listed as separate candidates). Track for a future code release before treating it as more than a direction-of-travel indicator.
